articles.title: No wildlife board nod, stop-work order issued to Adani company’s power project in Satara
articles.summary: Satara DCF orders Adani Renewable Energy to halt 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage work for lack of NBWL clearance; seeks tree-felling approvals and project papers.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The deputy conservator of forests (DCF), Satara forest division, has issued a stop-work order to the project manager of Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd, Mumbai, for starting work on the 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project in the district’s Patan taluka without prior approval from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).Adani Group said the proposal for wildlife clearance has been submitted to the board.The action by DCF Amol Satpute came after it was separately flagged in Oct that Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL), which is executing the project, had understated the project cost to the state govt, slashing it from Rs 5,675 crore to Rs 56.75 crore, to reduce its statutory environmental obligations.Issuing a show-cause notice on Nov 13 under Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and Maharashtra Tree Felling (Regulation) Act, 1964, the DCF sought a written explanation on the authority under which the project was initiated without the valid NBWL permission. He warned that if work continues at the site, strict legal and penal action would be initiated under the applicable forest laws.The notice asks whether permissions were obtained from the competent authorities for tree felling linked to the project. The company has been asked to submit the total number of trees approved for felling if such permissions exist, along with original or attested permits, and provide all related statutory approvals and project maps within the stipulated period.The reply was to be submitted to the range forest officer’s office within three days of receipt of the notice.An AGEL spokesperson said the necessary permissions/NOCs on land use and statutory requirements had been obtained from the competent authorities. The spokesperson said based on the environmental clearance granted in Feb 2025, Maharashtra Pollution Control Board issued the consent to establish on April 7, 2025 to allow the work to begin. “Construction activities commenced only after obtaining all the requisite approvals from the authorities concerned.”The company said the process for wildlife clearance has been duly initiated and pursued as part of the environmental clearance compliance process. “The proposal for survey and investigation activities was submitted in Jan 2025 and subsequently recommended by the state board for wildlife. The proposal for the project has since been submitted to NBWL and is currently under consideration. The project is being developed in full compliance with applicable statutory requirements and the directions of the competent authorities.”The spokesperson said no project component falls in any notified protected area or forest land, and that the NOC stating this was received on Jan 23, 2024.On Oct 30, Satara’s honorary wildlife warden Rohan Bhate had flagged an alleged discrepancy in the project cost declared to the state govt, stating it was shown as Rs 56.75 crore instead of Rs 5,675 crore. In representations to NBWL, the ministry of environment, forest and climate change (MoEFCC) and the CM, he sought an independent inquiry, arguing that an understated cost could amount to misrepresentation and could affect wildlife conservation contributions linked to the project value.MoEFCC’s environmental clearance issued on Feb 11, 2025, records the project cost at Rs 5,675 crore. It also lists Rs 39.3 crore as capital cost for the environment management plan and pollution control measures, and Rs 27.5 crore as recurring operation and maintenance cost.Reports also state that on Sept 7, AGEL chief operating officer Naresh Telugu submitted a letter to the principal chief conservator of forests (wildlife), Maharashtra, along with a notarised undertaking on a Rs 500-stamp paper, citing the project cost as Rs 56.75 crore. The undertaking reportedly said the figure was based on an “analogous estimation” used while submitting “Part IV,” requested authorities to consider Rs 56.75 crore as the project cost, and committed to mitigation and conservation measures.The company denied allegations of cost understatement to reduce statutory obligations, saying figures mentioned in the online forest and wildlife clearance proposal related only to preliminary investigations and surveys.In his letters, Bhate had said, “The difference between the estimated total project cost reflected in the available project documents and the amount stated in the notarised undertaking by AGEL is substantial. The two figures differ by a factor of 100. The administration of Sahyadri tiger reserve (STR) had communicated to AGEL well in advance that an amount equivalent to 4% of the total project cost, ie, approximately Rs 227 crore, was required to be deposited in the account of the STR Conservation Foundation for wildlife conservation and protection, subject to the applicable provisions and conditions.” He said based on the revised project cost of Rs 56.75 crore, an amount equivalent to 1% was calculated as Rs 56.75 lakh for payment. The remaining 3% was to be paid after NBWL’s clearance.“If the project cost has indeed been deliberately understated in the undertaking submitted to the state govt, the matter raises serious concerns regarding the possible misrepresentation of material financial information to govt and its consequential impact on the financial contribution required for wildlife conservation. Hence, it has been necessary to establish whether the project cost was correctly assessed, whether the applicable contribution requirements were properly implemented, and whether the decision to calculate the contribution on the basis of Rs 56.75 crore as revised project cost was supported by the relevant rules, official records and approved conditions,” Bhate had said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: US government proposes new rules for Green Cards; tells companies: American Workers are the best in the world, rule change will ensure they are …
articles.summary: The US government is proposing stricter rules for companies sponsoring foreign workers for employment-based Green Cards.
articles.body: The US government is proposing stricter rules for companies sponsoring foreign workers for employment-based Green Cards. The US Department of Labor says the changes will ensure that qualified American workers get the first opportunity to apply for high-skilled, high-paying jobs before companies turn to foreign workers. “American Workers are the best in the world, and they deserve the first and best job opportunities,” Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said while announcing the proposal. He added that the rule change would put American workers “first in line” for such jobs.The proposal seeks to overhaul the Permanent Labor Certification programme, also known as PERM. It is the first major update to the programme in nearly 20 years.For the unaware, PERM is an important step for many employment-based Green Card applications under the EB-2 and EB-3 categories. Before sponsoring a foreign worker for permanent employment, companies generally have to show that they could not find qualified US workers for the position and that hiring the foreign worker would not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of American workers. PERM approval itself does not grant a Green Card.What changes are being proposed to Green Card rulesOne of the biggest changes involves how companies advertise jobs. The Labor Department wants employers to move away from print-based advertisements and use modern recruitment methods. Under the proposal, companies would have to advertise vacancies through their websites, online job portals and social media platforms. They may also use job fairs and campus recruitment.Employers would have to keep job advertisements open for at least 90 calendar days. If they normally advertise similar positions for a longer period, they would have to follow that longer period. The department says this would give qualified American workers more time to learn about vacancies and apply.The proposal would also require companies to use the same recruitment channels and methods for PERM positions that they use for similar jobs that do not require labour certification. Employers would have to make genuine efforts to consider qualified US applicants and provide job-related reasons if they reject them.Companies that laid off US workers could face restrictionsThe proposed rules also target companies that lay off American employees while seeking to sponsor foreign workers. Under the proposal, employers would be barred from filing a PERM application if they had laid off US workers in the same or a similar occupation at the relevant work location during the previous two years.If a company lays off American workers after filing a PERM application, it would have to consider potentially qualified laid-off employees for the position. This requirement could continue until the related Form I-140 immigrant petition is approved or the case reaches a final decision.Employers would also have to inform the Labor Department, and the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) where applicable, about such layoffs within five business days.Nurses and physical therapists could also face new requirementsThe Labor Department has proposed ending the administrative exemptions under a system known as Schedule A. At present, certain occupations, including professional nurses and physical therapists, can bypass the usual labour market test under Schedule A. The exemption also covers certain individuals with exceptional ability in the sciences, arts and performing arts.If the proposal is adopted, employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers in these categories would also have to test the US labour market and consider qualified American applicants.When will the proposed Green Card rules take effectThe changes are not final yet. The Labor Department has invited the public to submit comments on the proposal for 60 days after its publication in the Federal Register on November 17.The proposal is part of the US administration's wider efforts to tighten employer-sponsored immigration pathways and strengthen protections for American workers. If finalised, the changes could make the PERM process more demanding for companies seeking to sponsor foreign employees for permanent residency in the US.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: Packers Get Crushing Report After Bad Loss to Vikings
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers got some unfortunate news following a 20-point defeat to the Minnesota Vikings. The post Packers Get Crushing Report After Bad Loss to...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are two games above .500 heading into their bye week, which should put them in a highly favorable position with regards to playoff contention come the end of the regular season, but the oddities of the NFC North in 2026 have rendered the opposite true.

Social media-based salary cap specialist Ken Ingalls, who focuses almost exclusively on the Packers, recently laid out the math on Green Bay's postseason chances — and the numbers are not good.

Everything went wrong for the Packers' playoff chances yesterday. Lions, Vikings, Rams, Seahawks win. Packers lose. Chance to make the playoffs dropped to 35%. Week 12 against the Rams is their largest impact game remaining on the schedule. 58% with a win / 23% with a loss.

Everything went wrong for the Packers' playoff chances yesterday.

Chance to make the playoffs dropped to 35%.

Week 12 against the Rams is their largest impact game remaining on the schedule. 58% with a win / 23% with a loss.

Packers Desperately Need Pass-Rusher Micah Parsons to Return to Action in Los Angeles

Those implications for Green Bay's Thanksgiving Eve contest against the Rams in Los Angeles make the injury status of pass-rusher Micah Parsons all the more critical to the Packers' chances of success, not only in moving to 7-4 on the season but of keeping their playoff hopes above water.

Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed in an interview session on Monday that the team intends to bring Parsons back into an on-field role against the Rams on November 25. But he also said the superstar outside linebacker isn't quite there yet.

"We'll see," LaFleur said of Parsons playing nine days from now. "There's still a couple more hurdles for him to clear before I think we can definitively say that he's a go. But he's been showing progress, and we'll see where he's at by the end of the week."

Parsons spoke with reporters earlier this month and was also unwilling to put a definitive stamp on his return timeline, saying he did not want to put more pressure on it than necessary or make a promise about playing that he was not sure he could keep.

Packers Face Scary Rams' Defensive Front After Bye Week

Parsons' return would undoubtedly prove an enormous boost to the Packers' entire team. But that said, it was not the defense that was the problem against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

Minnesota rolled the Packers in Green Bay by 20 points (30-10), but the true culprit was the Packers' four turnovers, and those were a direct result of the offensive line's inability to protect quarterback Jordan Love.

While it is true that the Vikings defense is the fiercest and most relentless unit in the entire NFL with regards to QB pressure, Minnesota leads the league with 37 sacks through Week 10, Green Bay was also woefully unprepared to stop its opponent in that regard.

The Packers have a week and a half to figure out the situation up front, as the likes of Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and several other elite-level defensive linemen who wear Rams uniforms will be waiting for them at SoFi Stadium just ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
